A risk assessment is not a one-time document. The CPPA's regulations require it to be updated when the processing changes in a way that matters (11 CCR § 7155(a)(3)). The Final Statement of Reasons gives the actual test: a change is material if it "creates new negative impacts," "increases the magnitude or likelihood of previously identified negative impacts," or "diminishes the effectiveness of safeguards." The Agency specifically rejected a narrower version of this test, saying the narrower wording would let more changes go unassessed. If this company's ADMT, its training data, its safeguards, or its decision use have changed since its last risk assessment, this standard — not a general sense that "nothing major happened" — is what decides whether an update was required. Whether that update was completed here is a fact about this company's own record. (California Privacy Protection Agency, Final Statement of Reasons, CCPA Updates, Cyber, Risk, ADMT, and Insurance Regulations, 11 CCR § 7155(a)(3), Appendix p. 148.)
